title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Monster Monday Swell Backs Off; Chips Paddle Back In
conditions.summary: Futures slip as chip stocks give back part of Monday's huge Nvidia-led rally, with the Nasdaq hit hardest. VIX is up and traders are bracing for Wednesday's PCE inflation report, with a December Fed hike now priced in.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures were down about 0.5%, Nasdaq-100 futures down about 1.2% and Dow futures down about 0.1% as of roughly 5:30 AM ET; earlier quotes were weaker, so readings are still moving.
Russell 2000 futures were down about 0.5% in an early, untimed quote.
Monday was huge: the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5%, the S&P 500 4.7% and the Dow 3%, the best day since April 2025, after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.92%; WTI crude is flat around $80; gold is off 0.6%; bitcoin is down about 2.5% near $59,800.
The VIX is up about 9% to around 29, a sign traders still expect choppy water.
Asia rallied: Japan's Nikkei rose nearly 4% and South Korea's Kospi more than 6%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.7%.
Europe is mixed and pausing as the tech rally fades; Sanofi is a notable gainer.
No US dollar index reading was available in sources checked this morning.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 8:00 AM CT: Case-Shiller home prices for September; consensus +0.2% m/m.
9:00 AM CT: Conference Board consumer confidence for November; consensus about 92.2, versus 91.7 last month.
Also today: Richmond Fed manufacturing index, FHFA home prices and a $70 billion 5-year note auction.
The Fed is in its blackout period before the December 9 meeting; futures now price a 25 basis point rate hike in December, with a small chance of 50.
Main event this week is Wednesday's 7:30 AM CT data dump: October PCE inflation (core seen +0.3% m/m, 3.4% y/y), Q3 GDP revision, durable goods and jobless claims, plus the Beige Book at 1:00 PM CT.
Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reported fiscal Q4 results after Monday's close; shares are down about 11% pre-market.
Before today's open: Medtronic, Analog Devices, Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Kohl's and Bilibili are due; Best Buy is expected to earn about $1.49 a share.
After today's close: Dell (expected $6.62 a share on about $49 billion in revenue, with a big AI server backlog in focus), HP Inc., Autodesk, Workday and CleanSpark.
Deere reports Wednesday morning.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: HPE (Hewlett Packard Enterprise): -11% — falling after its fourth-quarter results.
NVDA (Nvidia): about -4% to -5% — giving back part of Monday's 31% surge on Jensen Huang's return as CEO.
MU, AMD, MRVL (Micron, AMD, Marvell): -3% to -4% — chip stocks cooling after Monday's rally.
CRWV (CoreWeave): -5% — AI cloud names giving back Monday's surge.
NBIS (Nebius): -4% — same neocloud pullback; IREN is also down more than 4%.
Anthropic: about -4% — heading for a third straight decline since its market debut last week.

sections.title: Business News
items: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO about 11 days after he resigned; it is creating a national security and export controls committee and will hire a chief compliance officer, while an internal review continues.
Amazon is reported to be close to, or to have agreed to, a roughly $7.5 billion deal for AI startup Decart, whose software helps AI models run more efficiently on chips.
Oregon and Virginia sued SpaceX and related companies over sexualized images made by the Grok chatbot, seeking penalties and court orders.
The US added Singapore-based Megaspeed to its trade blacklist over alleged Nvidia chip exports to China; the company denies wrongdoing.
The New York Times reports SpaceX is selling computing capacity to AI rivals including Anthropic and Google.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 9:00 AM CT consumer confidence: a read on holiday-season spending mood.
Whether chip stocks hold most of Monday's gains; Nvidia's pullback sets the tone for the Nasdaq.
Dell after the close: its AI server backlog is a key test for AI demand heading into Wednesday's PCE report.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Gus the wonder dog is curled up on his beach towel, but I think he's awake. Give the lineup a holler, Gus! Thanks, buddy. Conditions this Dawn Patrol are poor, after a truly gnarly Monday swell. Yesterday the Nasdaq jumped six and a half percent and the S and P five hundred gained almost five percent, the best day since April of last year. Nvidia rocketed thirty-one percent after its board brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive. This morning the wave is backing off. S and P futures are down about half a percent. Nasdaq futures are down about one point two percent. Dow futures are down only slightly. Early quotes are still moving, so stay loose. The ten-year Treasury yield sits near four point nine percent. Crude is flat around eighty dollars. Gold is down a little, bitcoin is off about two and a half percent, and the VIX fear gauge is up near twenty-nine. Over in Asia, South Korea's Kospi jumped more than six percent and Japan's Nikkei rose almost four percent. Now that's a set worth riding. Gus, that calls for a treat! Here you go, buddy! Europe is mixed. On the weather map, Case-Shiller home prices land at eight A M Central, and consumer confidence at nine A M Central, expected near ninety-two. The Fed is quiet ahead of its December meeting, and traders now price in a quarter point rate hike. The big storm is Wednesday at seven thirty A M Central, with October P C E inflation, a G D P update and jobless claims. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. On the tide chart, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is down about eleven percent after its results. Best Buy, Medtronic, Analog Devices and Dollar Tree report this morning. Dell, H P, Autodesk and Workday report after the close. In the lineup, Nvidia is giving back four to five percent. Micron, A M D and Marvell are down three to four percent. CoreWeave and Nebius are down four to five percent. And Anthropic is off about four percent, heading for a third straight drop since its debut. Beach talk: Amazon is reported to be buying A I startup Decart for about seven and a half billion dollars. Two states sued SpaceX over Grok images. And Washington blacklisted Singapore's Megaspeed over alleged chip exports to China. Sets to watch today: consumer confidence at nine, whether chip stocks hold Monday's gains, and Dell tonight.
